newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares close higher on secondliners.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares close higher on secondliners.

text.p: Jakarta share prices closed higher on Monday despite weak regional markets following active trade in selected second-liners and blue chips, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 3.53 points, or 0.64 percent, to close at 552.74 points. Losers led gainers by 61 to 37, with 43 counters unchanged.

Brokers said local operators actively bought selected second-liners in the first session but took their profits in the afternoon, while some foreigners bought selectively from a few heavyweight stocks.
"Trade was moderate due to the holidays in Hongkong and the United Kingdom," one local broker said.

"Overall market sentiment was mixed, with some operators cautious on news that the government and Megawati Sukarnoputri may not reach an out-of-court settlement, while others waited for company first half results," one foreign broker said.

Cable manufacturer Jembo Cable topped the active list with 15.3 million shares traded. It rose to 1,150 rupiah in morning trade following serious market talk of a possible acquisition but closed down at 950 rupiah on profit-taking.

Berlian Laju Tanker was actively traded, rising 100 rupiah to 2,425 on a turnover of 11.3 million shares. Brokers said the rise was due to its strong first half result and possible higher earnings on government regulations allowing domestic firms to import vessels.
Blue chip Gudang Garam made significant gains. It rose 5.85 percent, or 475 rupiah to 8,600 rupiah on a volume of 656,000 shares.
Brokers said the rise was due to market talk of possible strong first half results which they heard could be announced this week. --- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364
